prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals a wide outdoor walkway flanked by multi-storey building walls on the left (~3–6 m) and right (~3–8 m), with a smooth bright-to-dark ground gradient receding from 1 m in the lower foreground to over 15 m in the dark background. Along the left side of the path, a low bollard light stands ~4–5 m ahead in frame 1 and approaches to ~1.5 m at the far-left edge by frame 5 (where it is partly cropped out of view), while a pedestrian stands ~2–4 m further ahead and slightly right of that bollard (~5–9 m from the camera wearer, facing away). In frame 3, the map sharply delineates the camera wearer's own outstretched left arm in the lower-left foreground at <0.5 m (within arm's reach), showing it occluding the mid-ground pavement—a boundary that is much harder to see in the dark RGB frame. Across the five frames, the increasing brightness of the bollard, building pillars, and pedestrian silhouette tracks the camera wearer's steady forward approach and slight rightward pan after lowering their arm in frame 4. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 2 where it completely misses the camera wearer's raised dark-sleeved arm, in frame 3 where motion blur erases the pedestrian and farther bollard into the dark background, and in the distant courtyard archway (>15 m) which is flattened into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is mostly empty across the dark nighttime scene, detecting masks only in frames 1 and 4 while leaving frames 2, 3, and 5 completely blank. In frame 1, it segments the pedestrian walking away on the left (~8–9 m from the camera wearer) as a 'person' and misclassifies the nearer glowing bollard post (~4–5 m away, ~3–4 m in front of and to the left of the pedestrian) as a second 'person'. In frame 4, as the camera wearer approaches, it again segments the pedestrian (~5–6 m ahead, facing away and not looking at the camera wearer) as a 'person', helping isolate their silhouette against the dark background where RGB contrast is low. However, in frame 4 it also misclassifies the nearer bollard post (~2.5–3 m ahead on the left) as a 'parking meter' and the farther bollard light just to the left of the pedestrian's legs (~6 m away, partially occluded by the pedestrian) as another small 'person'. The map is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the pedestrian in frames 2, 3, and 5, fails to detect the camera wearer's own outstretched arm and hand (<0.5 m, the only object within arm's reach) in frames 2 and 3, and provides no segmentation of the surrounding buildings or walkway.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons. In the RGB strip, a pedestrian is present ~5–9 m ahead on the left side of the walkway across all five frames, walking away with their back turned toward the camera wearer, while the camera wearer's own left arm and hand extend forward into the lower-left view (<0.5 m, within arm's reach) in frames 2 and 3 before dropping out of the lower frame boundary in frame 4. Because no keypoints are detected, the pose map contributes no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB image and cannot track the pedestrian's gait, facing direction, or the camera wearer's arm extension and retraction. This total failure highlights the unreliability of body and hand pose estimation under dark nighttime lighting, severe motion blur (frames 2 and 3), and medium-to-far viewing distances (>5 m) for the pedestrian.
